tool.name: NextDenovo
tool.description: string graph-based de novo assembler for long reads
tool.command: ## NextDenovo separates the number of concurrently running subtasks (parallel_jobs, ## pa_correction, seed_cutfiles -- all hard-wired to 1 in the configuration below) from ## the number of threads each subtask uses. Only the latter is derived from the cores ## allocated to this job, so the tool never runs more work in parallel than allocated. threads="\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" && ## ovl_sort aborts with 'Assertion `opts.thread >= 2' failed' below two threads, so the ## per-subtask thread count is floored at 2. Concurrency stays at 1, therefore a ## single-core job runs one subtask at a time instead of failing outright. threads=\$(( threads < 2 ? 2 : threads )) && ## Memory buffer of the overlap sort, in GB, from the memory allocated to this job. sort_mem=\$(( \${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-8192} / 1024 )) && sort_mem=\$(( sort_mem < 1 ? 1 : sort_mem )) && mkdir -p './read_files' && #for $index, $sample in enumerate($input_reads) ln -s '${sample}' './read_files/sample_${index}.${sample.ext}' && #end for ls './read_files' -1 | sed -e 's|^|read_files/|' > './input.fofn' && ## Substitute the runtime resource values into the configuration. The placeholders are ## unambiguous tokens so that no configuration *key* is rewritten (a plain ## `s/jobs/1/g` would also turn `parallel_jobs` into `parallel_1`, which makes the ## parser fall back to its default of 10 concurrent subtasks). sed -e "s/@THREADS@/\$threads/g" -e "s/@SORTMEM@/\$sort_mem/g" '${config_template}' > './configfile' && nextDenovo './configfile' && ## Corrected seeds are written per subtask; concatenate them into a single dataset. ## The glob is empty when no correction is run, hence nullglob and the /dev/null input. shopt -s nullglob && cat 02.cns_align/01.seed_cns.sh.work/seed_cns*/cns.fasta </dev/null > './corrected_reads.fasta'

configfiles.configfile:
[General] job_type = local job_prefix = nextDenovo #if $input_type == 'corrected' ## input_type = corrected forces the task to assembly-only, and task = assemble ## with raw input forces the full pipeline (see lib/config_parser.py _check()). ## Write the effective task so that the configuration matches the outputs. task = assemble #else if $task == 'assemble' task = all #else task = $task #end if rewrite = yes deltmp = yes ## Concurrency is kept at 1 and every subtask gets all allocated cores, so the ## number of cores in use never exceeds the job allocation. ## See https://github.com/Nextomics/NextDenovo/blob/v2.5.2/doc/FAQ.rst parallel_jobs = 1 seed_cutfiles = 1 input_type = $input_type read_type = $read_type input_fofn = input.fofn
[correct_option] read_cutoff = $read_cutoff #if $genome_seed.selector == 'genome' genome_size = $genome_seed.genome_size seed_depth = $genome_seed.seed_depth #else seed_cutoff = $genome_seed.seed_cutoff #end if blocksize = $blocksize sort_options = -m @SORTMEM@g -t @THREADS@ -k $ovl_parameters.max_depth_overlap -l $ovl_parameters.max_over_hang_length minimap2_options_raw = -t @THREADS@ --minlen $minimap_parameters.minlen --minmatch $minimap_parameters.minmatch --minide $minimap_parameters.minide --kn $minimap_parameters.kn --wn $minimap_parameters.wn --cn $minimap_parameters.cn --maxhan1 $minimap_parameters.maxhan1 --maxhan2 $minimap_parameters.maxhan2 pa_correction = 1 correction_options = -p @THREADS@ $correction_options.split $correction_options.fast
[assemble_option] minimap2_options_cns = -t @THREADS@ nextgraph_options = -a $np.a $np.c $np.G $np.k $np.A -E $np.E -q $np.q -i $np.i -I $np.I -R $np.R -S $np.S -r $np.r -M $np.M -T $np.T -N $np.N -u $np.u -w $np.w -D $np.D -P $np.P -m $np.m -n $np.n -B $np.B -C $np.C -z $np.z -l $np.l -L $np.L -t $np.t -F $np.F

param.option: Correct: only do the correction step
Assemble: only do the assembly step (only works if input type = corrected or read type = HiFi)

param.label: Input type
param.help: You can use raw or corrected reads.

param.label: Read type
param.option: HiFi: PacBio highly accurate long reads

param.name: read_cutoff
param.label: Read cutoff
param.help: filter reads with length smaller than read_cutoff

param.name: selector
param.label: Provide estimated genome size or seed cutoff
param.help: It is required to perform some simple statistics (such as length distribution, total amount of data and sequencing depth) on the input data

param.name: genome_size
param.label: Estimated genome size
param.help: Estimated genome size, suffix K/M/G recognized, used to calculate seed_cutoff/seed_cutfiles/blocksize and average depth, it can be omitted when manually setting seed_cutoff. Spaces are not allowed.

param.name: seed_depth
param.label: Seed depth
param.help: Expected seed depth, used to calculate seed_cutoff, co-use with genome_size, you can try to set it 30-45 to get a better assembly result.

param.name: seed_cutoff
param.label: Seed cutoff
param.help: Minimum seed length. Set it to 0 for calculating it automatically.

param.name: blocksize
param.label: Block size
param.help: Block size for parallel running, split non-seed reads into small files, the maximum size of each file is blocksize.

param.name: max_depth_overlap
param.label: Max depth of each overlap
param.help: This value should be equal or smaller than the average sequencing depth.

param.name: max_over_hang_length
param.label: Max over hang length to filter

param.name: maxhan1
param.label: Maximum over hang length for re-align

param.name: maxhan2
param.label: Maximum over hang length for filtering contained reads

param.name: split
param.label: Split
param.help: Split the corrected seed with un-corrected regions

param.name: fast
param.label: Fast
param.help: 0.5-1 times faster mode with a little lower accuracy.

param.label: Output alternative contigs
param.help: For highly heterozygous genomes, it will increase assembly size.

tool.help:
NextDenovo is a string graph-based de novo assembler for long reads (CLR, HiFi and ONT). It uses a "correct-then-assemble" strategy similar to canu (no correction step for PacBio HiFi reads), but requires significantly less computing resources and storage.
-----
# Input
- **Sequence reads**: one or more FASTA or FASTQ datasets (optionally gzipped) of raw or already corrected long reads. Reads shorter than *Read cutoff* are discarded; reads at least *Seed cutoff* long are selected as *seeds* for the correction step. - Provide either an estimated **genome size** together with a **seed depth** — NextDenovo then computes the seed cutoff from the sequencing depth of your data — or set the **seed cutoff** manually (set it to 0 to have it estimated from the input alone). - **Read type** selects the preset alignment and correction parameters; choose the one matching your data (ONT 1D, PacBio CLR or HiFi).
-----
# Task
- **All**: correct the raw reads and assemble the corrected reads. - **Correct**: only produce the corrected reads. This is the cheapest way to check that the input data and the seed cutoff are suitable for an assembly. - **Assemble**: only assemble, requires *Input type = corrected* (or HiFi reads).
NextDenovo normalizes impossible combinations: with *Input type = corrected* the task always becomes *assemble* (already corrected reads are not corrected again), and *task = assemble* with *Input type = raw* becomes *all*. The written configuration file and the returned outputs follow the effective task, not the literal selection.
-----
# Outputs
- **Corrected reads**: the consensus of the seed corrections, one FASTA record per corrected seed. - **Preliminary contigs**: contigs derived directly from the string graph. They can be used as the final result after validation, but may contain more errors than the final assembly. - **Assembly**: the final consensus assembly, produced by mapping the corrected reads back onto the preliminary contigs and calling a new consensus. - **Assembly statistics**: N10–N90, minimum, maximum and average contig length, and contig counts. - **String graph**: if the NextGraph *output format* is set to **GFA**, the graph is written as GFA2 and the run stops after graph construction — no FASTA assembly or statistics are produced. - **Configuration file**: the NextDenovo configuration exactly as executed, useful to reproduce or troubleshoot a run.
-----
# Resources
NextDenovo distinguishes the number of concurrently running subtasks from the number of threads each subtask uses. This wrapper always runs one subtask at a time and gives it all cores allocated to the job, so it never uses more cores than requested. Larger datasets simply take longer on small allocations; requesting several cores speeds up the alignment and correction steps. The memory allocated to the job is passed to the overlap sorting step.
# Tips
- A too high *Seed cutoff* discards seeds and can leave the assembly empty; a too low one makes the correction slow. Start with an estimated genome size and inspect the corrected reads output. - If the assembly is empty or heavily fragmented, raise *Minimum short branch length* (NextGraph `-q`, e.g. to 5) and check the sequencing depth of your data.
